All 40 services (service-000..service-039) were migrated to new primary regions after a maintenance window; the pre-migration region assignments in generation-0 memory are stale and must be superseded.

Evidence: “Update for lesson 0: service-000 was migrated to eu-west-1 after the maintenance window.”

When to use: When a transcript reports a service being staged or migrated to a region after a maintenance window.
Steps:
1. Ignore or discard the 'briefly staged in <region>' interim notice as transient.
2. Take the region from the 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' update as the new canonical value.
3. Supersede the existing region note for that service rather than adding a second note.
4. Update the consolidated region-assignment wiki page.

Migrations are announced in two parts: an 'Interim status: <svc> was briefly staged in <region>' notice, then 'Update for lesson N: <svc> was migrated to <region> after the maintenance window.' Only the final migrated region is durable; staging notices are transient and must not be stored as the service's region.

Operates a fleet of 40 services (service-000 through service-039) distributed across five AWS regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-south-1.

Evidence: “Update for lesson 20: service-020 was migrated to us-east-1 after the maintenance window.”

Only the 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' statement is authoritative for a service's current primary region; it supersedes any earlier value.

Evidence: “service-000 was migrated to eu-west-1 after the maintenance window.”

Interim 'briefly staged in <region>' lines are decoys: in 6 of 8 observed pairs the staging region differed from the final migration target, and in 2 pairs (service-010, service-035) they coincidentally matched — so the staging line is never evidence of the primary region, even when it happens to agree.

Evidence: “Interim status: service-010 was briefly staged in us-west-2”

When to use: When transcripts report region changes for many services, especially with 'interim staging' lines preceding 'migrated to ... after the maintenance window' lines.
Steps:
1. Collect only the 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' statements; ignore all 'briefly staged in <region>' lines.
2. Map each service-NNN to its migration target region, aggregating across every session (updates arrive in 'lesson N' batches).
3. Rewrite the single consolidated region table rather than creating one note per service.
4. Recompute the region distribution counts and update the 'Service region map' wiki page.
5. Archive or supersede any prior per-service region notes so stale values cannot be read.

Fleet region distribution after the maintenance cycle: eu-central-1 (12), ap-south-1 (9), us-west-2 (7), eu-west-1 (6), us-east-1 (6) — 40 services total.

Evidence: “Update for lesson 39: service-039 was migrated to us-west-2 after the maintenance window.”

Region-report interpretation rules: (1) 'briefly staged in <region>' is transient noise and never a primary region — even when it coincidentally matches the final target (service-010, service-035); (2) 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' is authoritative and supersedes any earlier value; (3) when a batch of migrations lands, rewrite the single consolidated region table rather than appending per-service notes.

The operator runs 40 services named service-000 through service-039, spread over five AWS regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-south-1. Region assignments change during maintenance windows; see the Service region map for current values.

Rules for interpreting region reports: (1) 'briefly staged in <region>' is transient noise, never a primary region — even when it coincidentally equals the final target; (2) 'migrated to <region> after the maintenance window' is authoritative and supersedes any earlier value; (3) when a batch of migrations lands, rewrite the single consolidated region table rather than appending per-service notes; (4) updates are spread across sessions in 'lesson N' batches, so aggregate all sessions before rewriting the map.
